card.title: 97th RIFLES

card.flavorText: The 97th Rifle Regiment was a unit of the 18th Rifle Division of the Soviet Red Army during WWII. The division was formed in 1918 and took part in the invasion of Poland in 1920, where it was defeated at the Battle of Warsaw. From 20 November 1939 to March 1940, during the Winter War, the division was assigned to the 56th Rifle Corps of the 8th Army. It led the attack along the Lemetti-Koirinoja-Imphilathi-Sortavala road, where it again got defeated by the Finns. It was disbanded shortly after. The 18th Division was reestablished in 1939 and was stationed in the city of Kazan when Operation Barbarossa started. The division fought against the German advance east of the Dnieper River, where it was encircled and only a small part of the division managed to escape. The 18th Division was established again in September 1941 and participated shortly after in the Battle of Moscow, after which it was raised to Guards status for its actions and renamed 11th Guards Rifle Division. In 1943 the division broke through the German encirclement of Leningrad and joined the Leningrad Front. In 1944 it took part in the Karelian offensive against the Finnish forces and later that year it participated in the East Pomeranian Strategic Offensive Operation and fought at Danzig, Poland. After the end of the war the 18th Rifle Division was stationed on the Danish island of Bornholm before being withdrawn and disbanded in 1946.
